title: Plural genitive of common -e words
summary: Use the stem ending in -e- before -iden or -itten: huone (“room”) → huoneiden.
objectives: Use the stem ending in -e- before -iden or -itten: huone (“room”) → huoneiden.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A plural genitive refers to more than one person or thing. Its ending belongs to the plural modifier, not necessarily to the thing owned. Here the task is forming the word.
Use the stem ending in -e- before -iden or -itten. Include consonant strengthening where the word requires it.
keyPoints: Learn the word with its stem; the last letter alone does not identify every pattern.

steps: Keep huone- and add -iden or -itten: huoneiden or huoneitten.
The form changes the grammatical use, while the word keeps its basic meaning.

practiceExercises.prompt: Complete the plural genitive of huone (“room”): huoneide____. Write only the missing letter.
